text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Insurer Delta Lloyd fails to form an alliance with health insurer Anoz. (p1)
- Public prosecutor starts investigation into possible insider trading in Toolex Alpha shares. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers tempers his criticism of general auditors office. (p1)
- European Commission to probe Dfl 25 million state subsidy for printer and copier maker Oce van der Grinten. (p1)
- Automotive components maker Polynorm takes 51 pct stake in France's manufacturer Blocfer. (p3)
- Transhipment companies Nedlloyd and P&O sign legally binding agreement for merging their container businesses. (p3)
- The Netherlands is heading for a lower budgetary deficit than expected this year in September's budget proposals. (p4)
- Retailer Ahold extends its credit facility from $400 million to $1 billion. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Ajax, Feijenoord and PSV oppose other 33 soccer clubs in their view that broadcasting rights belong to them and not to soccer association KNVB. (p1)
- National rail strike next Monday and Thursday, possibly even the whole week. (p1)
- Rapid growth in temporary employment comes to a halt in third quarter. (p2)
- Bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker able to continue production as long as suppliers want. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Uproar in Rotterdam police force over arrest quota needed for pay rise. (p1)
- Parliamentary parties' criticism on closely knit relation between government and businesses disappoints Aruba. (p3)
- Philips Electronics returns to PC market with hand-held personal computer. (p25)
- Air UK, 45 pct owned by Royal Dutch Airlines KLM, to start booking service via the Internet. (p25)
TROUW
- Cabinet has no plans to legislate over a maximum number of night flights to and from Beek Airport. (p4)
- British government hinders start of KLM flights to Kenya and those of partner Kenya Airways, according to KLM. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- ABN Amro bank buys Australian bank Lloyds NZA. (p11)
